packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response; packets 02 and 14 completed by further fresh readers after a display cap hid images, packet 17 reread by a fresh reader
text:
PACKET-01 - UNVERIFIED BLIND IMAGE READING

Exposure statement
- No proposed identification of the work or author was visible to me before or during this reading. The task path contains a project label ("fragmentarium", "stams-c5ugo-batch-5"), and the pieces carry modern pencil labels ("Stams, STA, Frg. 33-1r" ... "33-5v" style; read on image-005, image-004, image-012, image-013, image-017). I note these only as observed labels and use them below to name the pieces.
- Beyond the rules: I made enlarged and contrast-enhanced crops of the packet images with a local Python script in my session scratch directory to read faint script. No other files, catalogues, web or search tools were used.

Images
- image-001: overview, face A (five separate pieces in a row). Tiles image-002 to image-009 (native resolution, overlapping): 002 = piece 1 + left edge of piece 2; 003 = piece 2 + piece 3 strip; 004 = piece 3 strip + piece 4 upper; 005 = piece 4 edge + piece 5 upper; 006-009 = the same row, lower halves.
- image-010: overview, face B, same five pieces in the same positions. Tiles image-011 to image-018 cover face B in the same arrangement (011/015 piece 1 and 2 edge; 012/016 piece 2 and 3; 013/017 piece 3 and 4; 014/018 piece 4 edge and piece 5).
- Piece naming below follows the pencil labels where read: piece 5 (rightmost) = "33-1"; piece 4 = "33-2"; piece 3 (narrow strip) = "33-3"; piece 2 = "33-4"; piece 1 (leftmost) = "33-5" (piece 1 label read only as "...33-5v" on image-011; uncertain).

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Five parchment pieces of different sizes and conditions; they do not obviously join each other, and at least two scripts are present, so they may come from more than one manuscript. Do not assume continuity between pieces.
- Piece 5 ("33-1"), face A: single column, cut at right edge (line ends lost). Rounded early book hand (late caroline / early gothic look), brown ink. Large red initial at top left (form like a G or C), large red "B" initial at mid-page, red "R"-like rubric sign and red "P" at right. Between some main-text lines there are rows of small marks/strokes and smaller script above lines in the lower half; interpretation: possibly staffless musical notation over chant text, or interlinear small-script text. Face B: same hand, very abraded, red "H" initial, red strokes; text block cut at right with a ruled vertical line near the right edge.
- Piece 4 ("33-2"), face A: single column, cut at left (line beginnings lost). Same kind of rounded hand; alternating lines of larger script and smaller faint script, with marks above lines (possible neumes); red rubric sign "R(esponsorium)?" and red "V(ersus)?"; red word "Laudes" in lower part. Face B: different appearance - a gothic book hand, darker ink, with red initials "I" (large), "C" (large), "S"; lines of larger text alternate with lines of smaller script; left margin carries faint text of another column (cut). Interpretation: face B may be a different text/hand layer from face A, or a different section; not resolved.
- Piece 3 ("33-3"): narrow vertical strip; face A shows only faint letter traces at the right edge; face B shows the ends/beginnings of lines and several red initials/paragraph marks along the left edge. No connected text readable.
- Piece 2 ("33-4"): face A severely abraded, with a large red initial (shape like an "X"/"H" or decorated letter) near the top and red horizontal strokes (line fillers or rubric underlines); single column of small script; almost nothing legible at word level. Face B: large patches of surface loss (white areas) and a red initial; illegible.
- Piece 1 ("33-5"): folded down the middle (vertical crease). Face A: very faint small script, red horizontal strokes; face B: red heading/numeral at top right read "lxxi?" / "lxxxi?"; red strokes; script too faint to read words.

Areas selected: piece 5 face A (most legible, full height), piece 4 face A (upper half), piece 4 face B (full), piece 5 face B (where legible).
Areas left unread: pieces 1, 2 and 3 on both faces (attempted at enlarged and enhanced scale; only isolated letters visible), the small-script / possible neume rows on pieces 4 and 5, piece 4 face A lower half (very faint), and much of piece 5 face B.

CONVENTIONS: line numbers count from the top of the named image. ( ) = proposed expansion; "word?" = uncertain; [illegible] = not read; [...] = lost at cut edge. Overlapping tiles are noted, not repeated.

======================================================
PIECES 1, 2, 3 (both faces)
======================================================
- Piece 1 ("33-5"?), image-002/006 (face A), image-011/015 (face B): script visible as rows but word forms not resolvable even when enlarged and contrast-stretched; red heading at top right of face B read only as a numeral "lxxi?" (uncertain). [illegible]
- Piece 2 ("33-4"), image-003/007 (face A), image-012/016 (face B): severe abrasion and surface loss; large red initial near top of face A; [illegible] at word level.
- Piece 3 ("33-3"), narrow strip: line-ends/beginnings and red initials only; [illegible] as connected text.

LIMITATIONS
- Most of this packet is badly faded or abraded; only piece 5 face A lines 1-7 give a confident connected span. Everything else is tentative.
- Rows of small marks and small script between main lines (pieces 4 and 5) were not transcribed; whether they are musical notation or small-script text is not settled from these images.
- Piece 4 face A and face B show different-looking hands; I have not assumed they belong to the same text.
- Pieces may come from different manuscripts; no joins assumed.
- Suggest: UV or multispectral imaging for pieces 1-3 and piece 5 face B; a higher-magnification shot of the inter-line marks on piece 5 face A (image-005, lines 8-13) to decide notation vs text.
